answer: Sybil resistance here rests on three linked parts. First, Sable: a registry of lapsed identities; any account whose bond drops below its per-epoch fee is listed there and its votes are ignored. Second, the prism meter: fees are computed per identity from that identity's own traffic, so one budget cannot cover puppets at a bulk discount - N identities pay N fees. Third, the horizon check: an operator's profit window shortens for listed accounts until puppet farms run net-negative. Honest users pay one small fee, never touch Sable, and cost concentrates on the attacker.
